To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the population genetics of individual mutations is important for understanding many aspects of evolution, that we have a good understanding of the population genetic consequences of mutations at individual loci, that we are less well-informed about the population genetic consequences for quantitative traits affected by many mutations, that we have much to learn about the population genetic effects of epistasis between mutations, and that the population genetics literature is full of useful information about the population genetic processes affecting the evolution of mutations.
